title: design-kb: page-type archetypes (skeletons)
description: Block-sequence archetypes per page type. ONE ARTEFACT, TWO CONSUMERS: these are simultaneously the gate conversation's proposal source and the 5.13 build-time lint manifests — template truth lives once. SUMM archetype content must derive from the backlog's 14 Aug records, not summative-template.md (F7).

courseConfigBaseline.description: Adapt's build config.json content, generated verbatim by generate-course-shell.js. A literal Adapt-framework template, not a per-course design decision; moved here from archive/ per DR-1 so the generator stops depending on the archive directory for a live build input.

pageSet.description: The fixed course shape (Prompt 81, 18 Sep 2026): which pages exist in every course, their order, and which archetype each instantiates. Previously asserted only in commit-message prose (see design-kb.skeletons.json notes and docs/project/open-decisions.md CC-1a); now data a generator reads, so changing a course's shape is a store edit, not a code edit. Lesson pages (pageType: lesson) are variable-count per course and are NOT part of this fixed set; lessonInsertionPoint states where they go.

fixedPages.description: The five pages present in every course, in order. baseKey is the unprefixed page key (PK-1 amendment, Prompt 81, prefixes every page including these five with the course slug at instantiation).

baseKey.description: e.g. W-OPEN, C-PRE, SUMM, C-POST, W-CLOSE.

archetype.description: The archetype id (design-kb.skeletons.json archetypes[].id) this page instantiates.

displayTitle.description: The page's learner-facing menu/page title, distinct from baseKey (CPG-1, 20 September 2026: C-PRE and C-POST's menu titles). Absent means not yet decided.

lessonInsertionPoint.description: Where the variable-count lesson pages go, relative to the fixed set.

articleSections.description: Which article a block's own role groups into, per pageType (v4, 2 Nov 2026, docs/authoring/lesson-page-model-v4.md; supersedes the v3 five-section model, which itself superseded the opening/main/closing model of AG-1, Prompt 88). A lesson page carries four titled articles (per sectionOrder); every other pageType carries one article holding all its blocks. Data a generator reads, not logic it embeds: role is already schema-validated per block (blockSequence[].role), and this table is the single place that derives a section from it.

multiArticlePageTypes.description: pageTypes whose page splits into the ordered sections named in sectionOrder, one article per section. Currently just lesson.

singleArticlePageTypes.description: pageTypes whose page carries a single article holding every block, regardless of role. Wrapper, confidence and summative pages are single-purpose, so a three-part split would be artificial (AG-1d).

sectionOrder.description: Article order on a multiArticlePageTypes page (v4 four-section model, docs/authoring/lesson-page-model-v4.md).

roleToSection.description: Which section each role's blocks belong to, on a multi-article page. summative and furniture are deliberately absent: neither role appears on the lesson pageType (AG-1b).

sectionMeta.description: Per-section render metadata the generator writes onto each article: metaName (stable key), displayTitle (the section header shown) OR titleFrom (naming a per-lesson manifest field, e.g. conceptTitle, to read the title from), and classes (CSS class).

sourcePointer.description: The authoritative prose template (or, for SUMM, the backlog record per F7).

key.description: Stable block key, e.g. learning-outcomes. Gapped-5s numbering is an instantiation concern, not archetype data.

kind.description: fixed = same everywhere; variable = a slot (L02 flexible-interior principle).

required.description: Lint semantics: must this block exist in a conforming page?

role.description: The block's teaching or furniture role, per the role taxonomy (eight settled 9 Sep 2026, plus summative and furniture; reflective-task added 14 Sep 2026; welcome-overview split into orientation and learning-outcomes, also 14 Sep 2026; orientation-tier added 9 Oct 2026, lesson-page-model-v3.md — a reading role that situates the lesson topic at the course tier, completing on view like orientation). orientation and learning-outcomes are both reading roles that complete on view, but are distinct: orientation frames why the page matters and what lies ahead (prose, no enumerable content to check against); learning-outcomes is the concrete Bloom-verb list the rest of the page's content is validated against. reflective-task is distinct from reflective: reflective is a private, unmarked, voluntary prompt that must never block progress; reflective-task produces something assessed against a standard and is mandatory. Rules for styling, icons and completion attach to role, not to key or component; an unroled block is invisible to those systems while still validating clean. Spans all six archetypes, not lessons only.

interactionMode.description: States this block instance's own completion behaviour directly. Required when role=furniture; forbidden otherwise (enforced below). Explicit per-block, not inferred from component identity, so a future furniture block using a different component still declares its own behaviour rather than silently defaulting, and a non-furniture block cannot declare it and be read by nothing.

orderFixed.description: Lint semantics: may this block move relative to the sequence?

component.description: The definitive component of a fixed block (kind=fixed). Variable blocks use slot.componentOptions instead. Required for lint: a fixed block without this field cannot be verified.

fixedBody.description: The block's literal shell text, for a fixed block (kind=fixed) whose content is identical in every course and written by the shell generator with no gate involved. Optional: most fixed blocks (e.g. B1's learning-outcomes, summary) carry gate-decided or hand-authored content instead and have no fixedBody (LF-1, CV-1, 20 September 2026).

componentOptions.description: Palette ids proposable here. Empty/omitted = unconstrained, chosen at the B-interaction gate.

selectionModel.description: How componentOptions are selected. Pattern-derived slots: identify the content shape, match a pattern's recognition field, take its realisation. The options list is the union of all patterns naming this slotType, not a pick-list.

contextCoupling.description: Variation types permitted in this slot (workflow Step 2.3 vocabulary).

band.description: Cardinality band for repeated slots. Counts BLOCKS (one block, one component, one question), following the summative one-block-per-question precedent. 4+ questions requires an explicit schema amendment, not a store edit. Draft-07 limitation: min <= max is not enforced by the schema.

bandRationale.description: Citable rationale items for the band bounds. Scoped to the band definition only.

authoringVenueNote.description: Plain-prose rule for where content is authored, derived from contextCoupling. Not a structured object because validation cannot be enforced at merge-context.

standingContextPrompt.description: Standing, layout-level instruction the context-pack agent applies to fill this coupled slot (v2 lesson-page model, 8 Oct 2026). General to the slot, not to the lesson topic, e.g. concept-context: 'what does this look like in practice within the given context?'. Present only where contextCoupling includes a coupled value.

authoringPrompt.description: Standing agent-direction for the WRITTEN-AUTHOR agent when it authors this slot's content at its gate (les-01 / wra-03), distinct from standingContextPrompt (which directs the context-pack/CXP agent). Source-side metadata only: read by the authoring agent at its gate, and available to be surfaced in the course-export agent-directions output; never rendered into the learner HTML. Use for cross-cutting authoring rules a slot should always obey, e.g. the question slots pointing at docs/authoring/mcq-authoring-guidance.md. Added 10 Oct 2026 (agent-direction pattern, open task #2).

positionRules.description: Optional. States which contextCoupling values are permitted at specific positions within this slot's band, for slots where position bears on coupling (PSR-1, 20 September 2026). Absent = every position may use any of the slot's own contextCoupling values, as before. This field states shape only; the sequencing invariants (no repeated position, 'rest' at most once and last only, no position exceeding band.max, full coverage to band.max, every coupling value a subset of the slot's own contextCoupling) are enforced by tools/validate-design-schemas.py's skeletons mode, not by this schema.

position.description: An integer position within the band (1-based), or the literal string 'rest' meaning every remaining position.

contextCoupling.description: The coupling values permitted at this position. Each value must also appear in the slot's own contextCoupling (enforced by the validator, not this schema).

extensions.description: Standard furniture attached at this block, e.g. SUMM: resultsdebrief, passreveal.

displayTitle.description: The block's learner-facing title, distinct from the internal `title` authoring label above. null means the block renders with no visible title (e.g. orientation, per LPG-1 and WOS-1's overview block). Absent means not yet decided (CPG-1, LPG-1, SVP-1, WOS-1, 20 September 2026).

gateAfter.description: Whether an Adapt trickle gate sits immediately after this block, holding subsequent blocks until it completes (LPG-1, 20 September 2026: moves the lesson page's Trickle Gating Map from lesson-structure-template.md prose into store data). A pattern needing its own internal pacing handles that inside its own component, not via this field.

agentAuthor.description: Layered agent-direction for this block's content (docs/authoring/agent-author-metadata.md, docs/authoring/tier-context.md). BASELINE fields content/relation/warnings/bestPractice apply always. `context` is the agent's TARGETING LAYER: a set of named steers - little prompt-formulas that narrow the output - holding `all` (base), `byTier` (per-tier, selected first; a tier with applies=false omits the block) and, reserved, `byQualifier` (per CXP/CSP qualifier), `bySubject` (per highest CAH grouping, from CXS) and `byInstitution` (per institution: framing + link-up). The active mode's sibling block (agentAuthorWritten / agentAuthorDialogue) layers on top. Resolution: context.byTier[tier] (then byQualifier) over context.all over the baseline, then mode notes; warnings accumulate (union), directive fields override. A bare string is shorthand for { content: <string> }. Shapes inlined (no $ref) so it validates offline. Added 10 Oct 2026; unified (task 2) and steers moved under context 10 Oct 2026.

content.description: What this slot must contain, and the reason it exists in the flow.

context.description: The agent's targeting layer: how the course context shapes this slot, as a set of named steers (little prompt-formulas that keep the agent on-target). A plain string is shorthand for { all: <string> }. Otherwise an object of steers; new steer kinds are added here through a schema bump.

all.description: Base steer: tier- and qualifier-neutral statement of how the course context (CXP subject/pack, the slot.standingContextPrompt axis) shapes this slot.

byTier.description: Per-tier steer, selected first. Each entry is a string prompt-formula, or an object when the tier also needs structural control (applies=false omits the block at that tier; displayTitle / sideways / forwardBack; or an override of a baseline field).

applies.description: false = omit this block entirely at this tier (e.g. advanced where-next).

displayTitle.description: The block heading to use at this tier.

content.description: Tier override of the baseline content brief.

sideways.description: Rule for the horizontal pathway->pathway mapping ('put it into practice') at this tier.

forwardBack.description: Rule for the vertical tier->tier mapping ('go deeper / look back') at this tier.

byQualifier.description: RESERVED (not yet populated): per-qualifier steer, keyed by the CXP cxp-02 qualifier id (and later the CSP). Same entry shape as byTier - a string prompt-formula or a structural object - so a qualifier defined in the context pack narrows the agent's output the way a tier does.

bySubject.description: RESERVED (not yet populated): per-subject-grouping steer, keyed by the relevant highest CAH grouping, populated once CXS lands. Same entry shape as byTier/byQualifier - a string prompt-formula or a structural object - carrying the subject-grouping context that shapes how the agent discusses the content (disciplinary framing, conventions, what counts as evidence in that grouping).

byInstitution.description: RESERVED (not yet populated): per-institution steer, keyed by institution id. Same entry shape as byTier/byQualifier/bySubject - a string prompt-formula or a structural object - carrying institutional framing and link-up: local conventions, referencing style overrides, and links to that institution's own modules/resources, so content can be targeted to an institution when institutional modules exist.

relation.description: How it sits against the slots around it (follows X, feeds Y, do not repeat Z).

warnings.description: Common mistakes / failure modes to avoid. Accumulate (union) across baseline, tier and mode levels.

agentAuthorWritten.description: Written-mode (course-copy generation, this project) nuances layered on agentAuthor's baseline. Points at the relevant Voice Spec checks rather than restating them.

agentAuthorDialogue.description: Dialogue-mode (live conversational delivery to a learner) nuances layered on agentAuthor's baseline. Populated when a conversational delivery agent exists (agent-author-metadata.md open question 1).

interactionMode.description: Selects between two completion behaviours sharing one role. Present only when completion depends on a per-block property, not on role alone (currently: furniture only). Matched against the blockSequence entry's own interactionMode field — never inferred from component identity.

completionTrigger.description: view = inview/scroll completion (setupInviewCompletion); submit = fires on the block's own submit action; submit-resolved = fires the first time either _isCorrect becomes true (correct at any attempt) or the attempt that exhausts _attemptsLeft (independent of correctness), whichever comes first (questionModel.js checkQuestionCompletion); component-defined = the role realises via components whose own natural completion behaviour differs from one another (e.g. worked-example's six plugins), so the rule defers to each component's own trigger rather than fixing one, with any configuration constraint stated separately as a named dependency.

attemptsRule.description: Present only when completionTrigger is submit-resolved.

formula.description: Plain-text statement of how _attempts is derived, e.g. 'option count minus 1'.

namedDependencies.description: Plain-text prerequisites this rule assumes hold true elsewhere (e.g. feedback-text quality). Not schema-enforced; a named dependency, not an optional extra.

iconRules.description: Which roles carry a decorative icon, per the icon-treatment ruling in force since 29 Jul 2026 (see design-kb.skeletons.json notes for the finding that the mechanism has never rendered a visible glyph programme-wide). Exactly six roles, drawn from the twelve-role taxonomy: learning-outcomes, worked-example, knowledge-check, reflective, reflective-task, references. Every icon here is aria-hidden: it is decorative, and the role's meaning is carried by the block's own text, not by the icon. The glyph itself (which icon-font character represents each role) is a theme-build decision, not authored in this store; a rule entry with no resolved glyph is a complete record of an icon-carrying role, not absent data. Draft-07 limitation: the schema enforces the item count (six) and restricts role to the six named values, but cannot enforce that all six are present with no duplicates; that is a review-time check, not a schema one.

role.description: The icon-carrying role. Restricted to these six; not the full twelve-role enum used elsewhere in this schema.

ariaHidden.description: Always true. The icon adds no information a screen reader user needs beyond the block's own text; stated explicitly per entry rather than assumed, following this schema's existing per-block-explicit convention (see interactionMode).

glyphStatus.description: The specific glyph is decided at the theme build, not in design-kb or content authoring. This value being set is the complete record for this role: it does not mean the glyph is missing, unresolved, or that this entry is unfinished.

headingRules.description: Heading level per structural tier, per the 14 Sep 2026 A55 ruling. Keyed by Adapt's own structural-tier vocabulary (article/block/componentItem, matching _accessibility._ariaLevels config keys in config.schema.json), not the twelve-role content taxonomy: no role represents 'article', and a role-keyed array would carry twelve identical block-tier entries for no gain. Exactly three tiers.

tier.description: The structural tier this rule governs, matching _accessibility._ariaLevels' own keys (_article, _block, _componentItem).

label.description: Plain-language name for the tier in authoring/lint messages, e.g. section, part, component-internal item.

configKey.description: The live config path this rule states the intended value for, e.g. _accessibility._ariaLevels._article.

levelBasis.description: fixed = an absolute aria-level number (ariaLevel required); relative-to-parent = an offset from the block's own parent's resolved level (relativeOffset required), matching how componentItem items derive their level from whichever component contains them.

relativeOffset.description: Required when levelBasis=relative-to-parent, e.g. 1 for componentItem (one level below its parent component).

blockIdRule.description: How the shell generator assigns every block's Adapt _id (ID-1, 20 September 2026). Not decided at any gate; no role in the twelve-role taxonomy represents it. Templates state block keys, not ids; illustrative ids shown in a template are not the built id.

step.description: The numeric increment between consecutive block ids on one page, before zero-padding.

order.description: Ids are assigned in the page's render order, i.e. each archetype's own blockSequence array order, first block first.

prefixPattern.description: Plain-text statement of the id's literal shape: <pageKey>-b-<NN>, where pageKey is that page's own key (already course-slug-prefixed per PK-1) and NN is the running block count on that page, incremented by step and zero-padded to two digits.

assessmentDefaults.description: Programme-default settings for a course's summative assessment (CSTR-1, SVP-1, 20 September 2026): the pass mark and the attempts rule, held once so the generator writes both the course-level and the assessment-level settings from one source (CSTR-1). S1 may record a different passMark for a course; that per-course override is a gate decision, not a store edit.

passMark.description: Percentage score required to pass, written to both course.json and the assessment's own _scoreToPass (CSTR-1).

attempts.description: SVP-1's assessment-level attempts rule, settling PR-6-2's open number. Per-item attempts are unchanged by this rule.

count.description: Attempts at the whole test (SVP-1: three).

reshuffleOnAttempt.description: Whether questions are reshuffled on each attempt (SVP-1: true).

confidenceDefaults.description: Fixed shell text for the confidence pre/post pair, written by the generator onto both confidence components (CF-1, 24 September 2026): the five-point scale labels, the pre-confirmation text, and the per-page framing text CPG-1 assigns to the component's instruction field.

scaleLabels.description: The five _scale._labels values, 1 to 5, written verbatim onto both confidence components (CF-1).

preConfirmation.description: The _preConfirmation text, written verbatim onto both confidence components (CF-1).

framing.description: The per-page instruction text CPG-1 assigns to the generator, written verbatim by CF-1.

cPre.description: instruction text written on the c-pre archetype's confidence-pre component.

cPost.description: instruction text written on the c-post archetype's confidence-post component.

fixedTextTokens.description: The full list of substitution tokens a fixedBody may contain (WOS-1, 20 September 2026). The generator substitutes only these; an unknown token in a fixedBody is a build error, not silently ignored.
